description:
The query arms build list responses and blocked-reason mappings inline. This moves them, bare `jit query` and `jit status` to library handlers.

## Background

In `crates/jit/src/main.rs`, `QueryCommands::{Available, Blocked, Strategic, Closed}` construct `IssueListResponse`, `BlockedListResponse` and their `--full` variants inline, `Blocked` maps blocking reasons inline, and each renders its own issue-list copy; `QueryCommands::{Count, Divergence}` fall back to `CommandResponse`; `query all` and bare `jit query` call `run_query_all`, and `reject_parent_query_filters` rejects filters placed before a subcommand. `Commands::Status` (`jit status`) renders the state rollup. Filters arrive through the flattened `IssueFilterArgs` group.

A handler in `crates/jit/src/dispatch/` takes its parsed arguments and a `CommandContext` (the executor and the `OutputMode { json, quiet }`) and returns `anyhow::Result<Outcome<R>>`; one registration per group generates the group's dispatch and its schema response lookup. Success responses are types defined in the output module (`crates/jit/src/output/`) or output constructors wrapping a command-layer result, each deriving `JsonSchema` and a human rendering; list payloads are `ListEnvelope<K, T, E>` instantiations; failures are returned as errors that `jit::output::failure::classify` maps to one code and exit status; a non-zero findings result is `Outcome`'s findings variant, rendered under `--json` as the failure envelope with the report in `error.details` and its registered code as the exit status.

On main, `run()` in `crates/jit/src/main.rs` parses the arguments and calls `dispatch()` in `main.rs`, which holds the command match; the arms and inline code this issue places in `run()` live in `dispatch()`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `run()` dispatches `query all|available|blocked|strategic|closed|count|divergence`, bare `jit query` and `jit status` to handlers in `crates/jit/src/dispatch/query.rs`, and `main.rs` keeps no arm body or `reject_parent_query_filters` copy for them.
- [hard] REQ-02: `query all` and bare `jit query` call the one library-side filtered-list function rather than a copy.
- [hard] REQ-03: Each leaf returns its registered response type, list payloads (including divergences) are `ListEnvelope` instantiations, the blocked-reason mapping is an output constructor, human lists go through the shared issue-list renderer, and the schema names a typed response for every leaf.
- [hard] REQ-04: The handlers return failures as errors with no substituted code or `std::process::exit`.
- [hard] REQ-05: Where a leaf's exit codes change, its rows in `CommandSchema::generate_command_exit_codes` (`crates/jit/src/schema.rs`) state the new codes and `docs/reference/exit-codes.md` is regenerated.
- [hard] REQ-06: Human output, success payloads and exit codes of these leaves are otherwise unchanged, and the existing suites pass without weakened assertions.

## Notes

Design rationale: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/plan.md`; inventories with function and arm citations: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/investigation.md`.
title: Query and status commands move to library handlers
